messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: increased KV cache evictions and p99 token latency for rope-ntk models in us-west-2. Incident INC-2026-234 created.

oncall-bot: alert details: metric=kvcache.evictions/s spike to 12k, mem_used/gpu shard=92%, p99_gen_latency=2300ms (baseline ~180ms). Affected model: rope-ntk-longctx-v3 (prefetch=yaRN, sliding_window=8192).

maria: seeing same in the dashboard, KV cardinality jumped ~45x after the NTK-prefetch rollout at 18:20 UTC. Noted a simultaneous increase in continuous_batch queue length.

raj: confirmed. Symptoms look like prefetch produced a huge number of unique prefix keys, eviction churn overloads rope shard. continuous batching amplified token fanout (many small batches with large context).

maria: quick check — customer-facing requests from acct-42 show p95->p99 tail. Tina, are we getting support tickets?


tina: yes, customer support flagged two active customers with timeouts to the API and 5xx from the backend gateway. They're asking for workaround. I told them we're on it and will update in 15. cc @support-eng.

carlos: can we throttle prefetch or revert the feature flag? We should avoid full rollback if possible.

raj: recommendation: 1) disable yaRN prefetch at the routing layer (soft off) 2) lower continuous_batch.max_delay_ms to 2ms 3) enforce per-model kv_max_entries=100k as temporary cap 4) enable fallback to shortctx variant for heavy requests.

maria: I'm patching the routing flag now.

maria: /api/flags/patch POST payload:
```json
{ "flag": "prefetch.yarn.enabled", "value": false }
```

maria: sent. waiting for propagation across edge.

kevin-sre: also applying batch config tweak on serving nodes:
```yaml
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_delay_ms: 2
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
```

kevin-sre: running playbook step to update config on the fleet (rolling). kubectl cmd:
```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/rope-serving --selector=pool=ntk-ropes
```

raj: setting kv cap via admin API:
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/models/rope-ntk-longctx-v3/kv-cap -d '{"kv_max_entries":100000}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

oncall-bot: propagation notices: flag patch propagated to 3/3 regions, batch config updated to 60% of nodes, kv cap applied to 100% of rope-ntk pods.

maria: seeing kvcache.evictions drop immediately, mem_used falling back to ~65% after ~90s. p99 latency trending down but still elevated.

tina: customers updated: acct-42 has lowered error rate, engineering contact acknowledged the temporary mitigation. Support sent a notification to the affected list.

carlos: we should still plan a rollback of the NTK prefetch rollout until we root-cause. Can we do a canary rollback for v3 only for high-traffic shards?

raj: agreed. I'll start a selective rollback for shards with >60% evictions/sec. Command:
```bash
redwoodctl rollout revert --model rope-ntk-longctx-v3 --filter shard.traffic>60
```

raj: revert started at 18:28 UTC; will take ~4 minutes per shard. Monitoring.

kevin-sre: note — continuous_batching config change reduces throughput; we're seeing CPU bump on driver pods, but that's preferable to thrashing the KV.

maria: logs from rope-serving-12 (pre-revert):
```
[E] kv_eviction: evicted_key_count=41234, cache_size=1.2G, reason=cardinality_exhaust
[I] batch_dispatch: dispatch_size=3, latency=2100ms
```

raj: post-revert stats: kvcache.evictions/s down to 120, p99_gen_latency back near 240ms, p95 ~85ms. Not fully back to baseline but acceptable.

tina: support confirms no open escalations for the impacted customers, they want an incident summary for the postmortem.

maria: creating an incident ticket: INC-2026-234, severity=sev2, impact=multi-tenant elevated latency and intermittent 5xx for a small subset of accounts. Attaching logs and diff of flags.

maria: immediate actions recorded: disabled yarn prefetch, lowered batching delay, applied kv cap, selective rollback of rope-ntk-longctx-v3 on high-traffic shards, monitor.

carlos: follow-ups: 1) postmortem to include reproduction steps and root cause (prefetch interaction with sliding-window + continuous batching), 2) enforce load test for prefetch rollouts, 3) add auto-throttle if kv_evictions > threshold.

raj: adding one more—add an early-warning metric: ratio unique_prefixes/total_requests > X should auto-disable prefetch. I'll stub the alert.

support-eng: notified customer success and sales for a proactive outreach. Template sent to CS: short summary + ETA for permanent fix.

oncall-bot: status update: incident moved to mitigated at 18:40 UTC. Next oncall: @kevin-sre for postmortem write-up.

kevin-sre: taking handoff. I'll own the postmortem, will include mitigation timeline, customer impact, telemetry graphs, and planned remediation (rate-limits, rollout gating, and a KV safety cap).

maria: thanks team. leaving notes: 1) do not re-enable yarn prefetch until we have stricter kv caps and rollouts gated by unique_prefixes alert. 2) schedule a QA load-run with longctx scenarios.

raj: filing follow-up tasks and linking to the code change PRs. PRs: #4589 (prefetch), #4592 (batching tweak).

kevin-sre: postmortem draft ETA: tomorrow 12:00 UTC. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:

support-eng: closing external comms loop. customers notified and monitoring.

maria: final note — we observed that sliding_window=8192 combined with prefetch policy caused per-request kv key expansion. Proposed permanent fix: cap prefetch fanout and add LRU segmenting per user.

oncall-bot: thread closed for active mitigation. Incident record: INC-2026-234, mitigated, follow-ups assigned.
